common_mistakes.mistake: Only one hero pushes the heavy parcel, or the two push from opposite sides/directions.
common_mistakes.consequence: The heavy crate does not move under a single pusher, so WEIGH never reaches its required load and loading_gate stays closed.
common_mistakes.recovery: Reposition both heroes on the same side and push in the same direction together; no failed-push recovery trace was recorded.

confidence_reason: Current source specifies the two-person heavy-crate rule, pad dependencies, bridge collapse, and slime death; a registered-source route reaches both exits with zero deaths. No failure/retry or human first encounter was observed.

confirmed: The weigh and team labels indicate a load threshold; the heavy parcel plus two-player push is the actual way to activate WEIGH.
Pac STEADY and Isp RESCUE are the intended bridge roles.
The central slime is a meaningful hazard, and the bridge is the required safe crossing.
missed_mechanics: A heavy parcel can move only with two connected heroes pushing in the same direction; its weight 2 then activates WEIGH.
Pac’s STEADY pad stabilizes the bridge and opens Isp’s crossing; Isp’s RESCUE latch permanently stabilizes the bridge and opens Pac’s dispatch route.
The bridge collapses after 0.8 seconds without stabilization and resets after 2 seconds; slime overlap is lethal.
incorrect_inferences: The first pass wondered whether WEIGH’s “2x2” meant a combined load or another object. It is a weight-two threshold; a heavy crate supplies that weight but requires two players to push.

The first pass treated the visible bridge position as evidence against timing pressure. Source shows a collapse timer, but the intended route stabilizes the bridge before crossing, so the timer is mainly a consequence of misordering.
changed_judgments: Reasoning remains 3: players must combine the heavy-parcel threshold with a held stabilization role and a latched rescue handoff.
Cooperation remains 3, now supported by two-person heavy-crate pushing and the Pac-to-Isp stabilization handoff rather than inferred “team” text alone.
Execution remains 2 because the route requires precise alignment and movement but the stabilized crossing itself is level and does not demand sustained jumps.
Timing rises from 0 to 1 because an unsupported bridge collapses after 0.8 seconds; Pac’s steady pad removes a narrow crossing window in the intended route.
Hazards resolves from null to 2 because the slime harms both heroes below the mandatory bridge, with stabilization as a safe approach.
Recovery resolves from null to 2 because a collapse into slime can reset the run and require repeating parcel/pad setup; no failed recovery replay is available.
Solution clarity remains 2: visible labels cue pad functions, but the two-pusher requirement and exact stable handoff are not fully explained without the optional hint.
unresolved: No novice attempt shows whether players recognize heavy means two pushers or maintain Pac on STEADY until RESCUE latches.
No collapse/death/retry trace quantifies recovery time or human cost.
Shared-keyboard reliability and actual coordination remain unknown.

single_operator_note: One operator would need simultaneous same-direction inputs from both heroes to push the heavy parcel, then hold Pac on STEADY while separately steering Isp across; this additional control interference is excluded from the two-human baseline.
